newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes rise on WTI, tighter discount.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes rise on WTI, tighter discount.

text.p: Prices for U.S West Coast crude rose with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) and higher diffs Friday, after players confirmed a Texas-based seller of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude sold at $-0.80 under WTI Thursday.
The alleged buyer and seller decline to confirm spot ANS trades, but several traders said 500,000 barrels sold at $0.80 under WTI, 10 cents higher than the last deal.
Outright ANS prices stood $20.45/20.65, up 45 cents on the combination of a lower discount and higher outright WTI values.
Line 63 stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, withprices on a fixed basis at $19.15/19.35 cents.

Kern River heavy crude prices rose after postings climbed Friday. Traders said California oil companies raised postings in anticipation the region's refiners would soon return from maintenance shutdowns.
